current_bottleneck: The clean unified path model preserves support, cross-cell structure, and joint anchor-factor realism, but neither plain flow-matching MSE nor a minimal full-path energy-score fine-tune learns the IV conditional location/dispersion allocation needed for coverage, conditionality, and tails.
last_result_summary: 648a fine-tuned 647a with a minimal full-path energy score in generated mixed-coordinate space, anchored by FM. IV score stayed 4/11 but worsened materially: cov90 66.3%->54.0%, conditional MAE reduction -0.7%->-12.7%, level-KS pass 10/25->1/25, median-bias pass 14/25->3/25. Pathwise max-jump KS improved slightly 0.618->0.575 but still failed. Joint audit also regressed: factor KS mean 0.087->0.115, factor KS pass 13/13->12/13, factor q99 pass 11/13->10/13.
next_step_recommendation: Do not continue by increasing energy weight, temperature, or factor-specific branches. Run post-experiment analysis/ideation on how to cleanly parameterize conditional location and dispersion jointly inside the path law, because the current objective can push spread but creates level bias and damages coverage.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 612a is the highest IV-count native joint run at 6/11 but has a degenerate source-scale mechanism and poor anchor-factor joint audit. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 641a is the clean native joint baseline because it removes post-hoc gluing and recovers strong anchor-factor realism, but it is still only 4/11 on the IV suite.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
